newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end down, hit by political drama.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end down, hit by political drama.

text.p: Fresh political squabbles within India's coalition government dragged Indian stocks down on Friday, and traders said the market was likely to weaken further next week.
End-of-account considerations at the Bombay exchange forced operators to square-off long positions amid dull activity on account of a holiday at the National Stock Exchange.

"There was no follow-up buying from players due to adverse political news," said a dealer at a foreign broking firm. "Foreign funds were select buyers. Thus, the market got cornered today on all fronts."

Laloo Prasad Yadav, leader of the breakaway Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) group of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party, on Friday asked three supporters to resign from Gujral's cabinet, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The splinter RJP group was created after Yadav refused to resign over a corruption scandal.
Later, after the market closed for trading, PTI reported that Yadav had retracted his decision and asked his three nominees on the cabinet to continue.
Earlier, shares marked time after news that the United Front's four-day old crisis, prompted by a regional party's threat to quit Gujral's government, had been settled.

But the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam party which threatened to pull out of the coalition, citing differences with partners, retorted on Friday that the problem had not ended and would be discussed further at a coalition meeting on July 25.
Analysts said on Friday that give-and-take seemed to matter little in the alliance because it was perched on a powder-keg of explosive political relationships.
"Any small accident can bring down the government. And accidents you can't predict," political columnist Kewal Varma told Reuters. "It can break any time. Such stresses and strains it cannot absorb."
